title: Safe Core: Players Who Fit Every Build
brief: Which players help in most categories without forcing a punt, so they suit the balanced build recommended for a 12-team auction? Tiers must be by price range, with a note on which stable categories each one provides.
summary: For the balanced build, fill your core from players ranked about 25 to 75 who have no weak category. Spend mostly in the 20 to 30 USD and 10 to 20 USD tiers, then add deep values like Ryan Rollins, Nickeil Alexander-Walker and Ty Jerome. When two players cost the same, take the one whose value comes from points, rebounds and assists over the one who relies on steals, blocks and percentages, because those counting stats repeat more reliably from week to week.

sections.heading: What the balanced build asks for

paragraphs.text: The balanced build skips the projected top 20. It puts the 11 core players in roughly ranks 25 to 75. Its ceiling is lower, but it is much safer. In our auction, that means not chasing the 60 USD and higher stars. Spread the money over many mid-priced players instead.

The safety comes from replacement. If your best player gets hurt, replacing a 30th-ranked player from waivers is much easier than replacing Jokic. With 144 players drafted, a lot of useful players stay on waivers. Keep some FAB for that.

Every player in this article has no weak category, so none of them forces a punt. Within that group, prefer players whose strengths are points, rebounds and assists. These high-volume counting stats are the most stable from game to game. A player who wins on steals, blocks and percentages repeats his value less reliably.

sections.heading: Where to spend in each price range

paragraphs.text: Above the balanced range, at 35 USD and up: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Jamal Murray fit every build. But Gilgeous-Alexander is a top-4 pick, and experts project Murray as a top 12 to 14 finish. Buying either one moves you toward a stars build. If you do buy one, keep Gilgeous-Alexander in the high 60s at most and Murray in the mid to high 30s.

The 20 to 30 USD tier is the heart of the build. Trey Murphy III (mid-20s), Jalen Williams (20 to 25 USD), Kawhi Leonard (stay near the 24 USD cap) and Chet Holmgren (about 21 to 22 USD) all sit in or near ranks 25 to 50. Their prices hold up only at those limits. Let someone else pay 30 USD for Holmgren or 29 USD for Williams.

The 10 to 20 USD tier is where most of the 11 core spots get filled. Experts see Alexander-Walker as a top 35 to 50 player, and bids up to about 20 USD are supported. Kyrie Irving is worth high teens. Buzelis runs about 15 to 22 USD, Anunoby 15 to 18 USD and Herro 14 to 16 USD. Naz Reid, Okongwu, Wagner, Porter Jr. and Ware fit at about 10 to 15 USD.

Below 10 USD you can still find rank 50 to 80 players. Rollins finished around 51st last season, and his market price is about 2 USD. Jerome, Coward, Fox, Powell, Harper and McDaniels are all fair at about 5 to 8 USD. From 1 to 4 USD, use Podziemski, Hart, Keegan Murray, Wiggins and Collins as late fillers that fit any build.

Scoring is the most common stable strength in this group. Murphy, Leonard, Alexander-Walker, Irving, Herro, Wagner, Knueppel and Powell all help PTS. Most of them also add threes and FT%. Murray and Jalen Williams add assists to their points.

For rebounds, Holmgren and Ware are the bigs to target, and both also help BLK and FG%. Porter Jr. adds rebounds from a forward spot. For assists, look at Rollins, Jerome, Fox and Harper at guard. Hart and Podziemski give both rebounds and assists. Those two categories are not usually linked, so combining them carries extra value.

Some players have no weak category, but their value comes mostly from steals, blocks or percentages. Anunoby (steals and threes), McDaniels (blocks, steals, FG%), Buzelis (blocks and threes), Okongwu (threes and steals) and Naz Reid (threes and blocks) belong here. They still fit, but treat them as the less stable part of your core. Do not overpay for them when a points, rebounds or assists player costs the same.

The method notes agree on the build. The disagreement is between the experts and the market. Experts say ESPN's 40 USD value for Leonard is too high and cap him at 24 USD. ESPN buyers pay only about 25 USD for Murray, while Yahoo's average cost is 39 USD. Experts put Knueppel in the 60s even though the market ranks him in the 30s and 40s. They see Holmgren in the 40s, not Yahoo's 31. On the other side, experts rank Alexander-Walker, Rollins and Irving well above what the market pays. Use the expert price caps, and treat the low market prices as your chance to buy.

sections.heading: Checks before the draft and in the playoffs

paragraphs.text: Before 2026-10-18, check the injury tags. Look at Holmgren's quadriceps (Q), Irving's knee (Q), Buzelis's ankle (Q), Porter Jr.'s wrist (Q), Fox's Q tag, and whether Gilgeous-Alexander's Q (Rest) tag is just preseason rest. Strus is listed Out with a foot injury.

A balanced build also needs games played in weeks 19 to 21. Toronto has three back-to-backs in our playoff weeks, which hurts Leonard. Dallas has a league-high 16 back-to-backs, so Irving could play only 10 games in his 4-4-4 playoff schedule if he keeps resting. Memphis's 4-4-4 schedule helps Jerome and Coward. McDaniels has a two-game semifinal week, and Houston has a weak 10-game playoff schedule for Sheppard.

Over the first 30 or so games, the Knicks plan to limit starter minutes. Track Anunoby, Hart and Bridges. Watch trade news before the 2027-03-04 deadline for Murray, Powell, Herro and Rollins. A trade to a contender would gut Powell's value before our playoffs.
